title: A bifunctional RNase H protein supports DNA replication and transcription in nucleus-forming Chimalliviridae phages
authors: Phoolwanti Rani; Niklas Klusch; Shannon Barret; Taylor Forman; Makaela Levine; Margot Riggi; Caroline Rees; Rui Liu; Lizbeth Hoffman; Meline Norquist; Dwaipayan Basu; Koe Inlow; Emily G Armbruster; Chase J Morgan; Joe Pogliano; Kevin D Corbett; Elizabeth Villa
one_liner_zh: 该文研究噬菌体RNase H蛋白Rhc在DNA复制和转录中的功能，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作但非TF-DNA体系，且以实验为主，无AI或物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Jumbo bacteriophages of the Chimalliviridae family replicate their genomes within a proteinaceous phage nucleus that spatially segregates viral DNA replication and transcription from translation. While the phage nucleus protects viral DNA from host defenses, it also imposes unique constraints on genome replication and gene expression. Here we identify the phage-encoded protein Rhc (RNase H-clamp) as a central mediator of genome transactions within the phage nucleus. Using the Escherichia coli infecting bacteriophage Goslar, we show that Rhc functions as an essential component of a non-canonical three-subunit DNA polymerase complex composed of DNAP N , DNAP C and Rhc. Rhc physically interacts with the DNAP C subunit, and both the catalytic activity of Rhc's N-terminal RNase H domain and its C-terminal sliding clamp-derived DNA binding domain are required for genome replication, nuclear maturation, and productive infection. Further, Goslar Rhc also supports transcription within the phage nucleus through a function that is separable from its DNA replication function. Rhc depletion results in reduced transcription of a subset of late genes, in a pattern that suggests a role for Rhc in resolving R-loops. Imaging and cryo-electron tomography reveal that loss of Rhc arrests phage development at a nascent nuclear stage, uncoupling nuclear assembly from maturation. Together, these findings identify Rhc as a multifunctional nuclear factor that mediates both DNA replication and transcription in nucleus-forming jumbo phages, revealing how viruses repurpose a conserved enzymatic activity to coordinate gene expression within a compartmentalized replication environment.
abstract_zh: Chimalliviridae家族的大型噬菌体在蛋白质性质的噬菌体核内复制其基因组，该核在空间上将病毒DNA的复制和转录与翻译分隔开来。虽然噬菌体核保护病毒DNA免受宿主防御机制的侵害，但它也对基因组复制和基因表达施加了独特的限制。在此，我们鉴定出噬菌体编码的蛋白Rhc（RNase H-钳夹）作为噬菌体核内基因组交易的核心介导因子。利用感染大肠杆菌（Escherichia coli）的噬菌体Goslar，我们表明Rhc作为非经典三亚基DNA聚合酶复合物的必需组分发挥作用，该复合物由DNAP N、DNAP C和Rhc组成。Rhc与DNAP C亚基发生物理相互作用，且Rhc N端RNase H结构域的催化活性及其C端滑动钳衍生DNA结合结构域均为基因组复制、核成熟和有效感染所必需。此外，Goslar Rhc还通过一种与其DNA复制功能可分离的功能支持噬菌体核内的转录。Rhc耗竭导致部分晚期基因的转录减少，其模式提示Rhc在解决R环中发挥作用。成像和冷冻电子断层扫描揭示，Rhc的缺失将噬菌体发育阻滞在新生核阶段，使核组装与成熟解偶联。综合来看，这些发现将Rhc鉴定为一种多功能核因子，在核形成型大型噬菌体中介导DNA复制和转录，揭示了病毒如何重新利用一种保守的酶活性在区室化复制环境中协调基因表达。
